scope: Disposable empty local PostgreSQL 16/pgvector database; no existing product archive used

web.runtime: Local Windows production standalone on loopback HTTP with restricted application database URL
web.browserUsed: headless Chrome behind ephemeral loopback HTTPS proxy

backupRestore.source: Disposable fresh pilot database after restricted CLI account provisioning and synthetic company write
backupRestore.restoreTarget: Second disposable database in the same local PostgreSQL cluster

diagnosticAttempts: First verifier read directly through the login role and received permission denied; the product intentionally switches to network_copilot_app inside a transaction.
Second verifier expected zero app_user rows; migration 003 creates a fixed placeholder with no password. Final verifier checks its exact ID, email and null password.
First browser run timed out after login because the raw local standalone directory lacked .next/static. The local verifier now copies generated static assets as Dockerfile.pilot-web does.

Second browser run returned login 401. A client hydration race was suspected; after waiting for network idle before filling the controlled form, the final run passed. The exact cause of that one 401 was not independently proven.
limits: Local empty-schema, service-layer, loopback HTTP, test-browser HTTPS and same-cluster backup/restore engineering proof only. Synthetic fixture accounts used random temporary passwords; all fixture data, both databases and archive were removed. The browser ignored a self-signed local certificate. No target cloud host or new-cluster restore, trusted HTTPS domain, real team network or account, concurrent use or later real-business-data migration was tested.
